subject: Clarify: where subscriber PII is processed and cross-border transfer
messages:
From: John Carter <john.carter@subscribly.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Question about where subscriber PII is processed

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the product walkthrough earlier. Two quick questions from our privacy and engineering teams as we assess a pilot:

1) For our use case (subscriber profiles + churn signals), where does Redwood process and store subscriber PII by default when using the Hosted API? Specifically: region(s), persistent storage vs ephemeral processing, and any backups/transfers.

2) Which subprocessors see request payloads or logs (names and region location if possible)? Do you use any third-party model execution partners that may be outside the US?

3) If we need guaranteed US-only processing (no transfer outside continental US), what are the options and how do you operationalize that?

Also our legal team asked for expected timelines on deletion if we call your deletion API and whether cached prefixes / KV caches are removed immediately.

Appreciate a short written summary so I can forward to Legal. If easier, happy to set a 30-min call.

Best,
John

Subscribly

Subject: Re: Question about where subscriber PII is processed

Hi John — thanks for the clear list. Summary below and I attached a processing map and our subprocessor inventory for more detail.

Short summary (for Subscribly pilot):
- Hosted API: production inference and transient request processing occur in AWS us-west-2 and us-east-1 by default (customer requests are routed based on load and latency). No customer data is served from EU regions unless the account is specifically provisioned for EU residency.
- Storage: We do not persist raw request payloads as long-term storage by default. Logs and operational telemetry are retained per account settings; default retention is 30 days for request traces and 90 days for aggregated metrics. Backups (metadata/backups of config) may be stored in AWS in the same region as the account.
- Subprocessors (high-level): AWS (compute + S3; US regions indicated), GCP (secondary backups for some internal services; US-based buckets where relevant), Datadog (monitoring traces, US datacenter), Sentry (error reporting), and a managed KMS provider for key escrow. Full vendor list and region locations in the attached CSV.
- Third-party model execution: We run model inference on our own runtime across our dedicated GPU pools. We do not route inference to third-party model execution vendors for production Hosted API customers.

US-only requirement options:
- Hosted: by default we use US regions; however load-based routing can fail over cross-region. For strict US-only processing we recommend Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Private (VPC) deployment. Dedicated can be provisioned in a single US region with no cross-region fallback. Private (VPC/on-prem) keeps all processing within your network.

Deletion / cache behavior:
- Deletion API: request to delete customer data triggers immediate eviction from in-memory KV caches and a background job to remove persisted traces and logs.
- SLOs: active caches evicted within seconds; persisted logs and backups deleted per retention pipeline — we target 30 days for full removal from backups, with an auditable workflow showing deletion steps. We can tighten those windows contractually for enterprise deals.

Next steps: happy to loop in Marcus (cc'd) from Security to answer questions about key separation, KMS, and audit logs. I can also send our standard DPA and SCCs.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Sales Director, Redwood Inference

From: Legal Ops <legal@subscribly.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-16T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question about where subscriber PII is processed

Evelyn — thanks for the helpful summary. A few follow-ups from our counsel:

1) Can you confirm whether model weights or any training telemetry are ever shared with a subcontractor located in the EU or APAC? Essentially, any time a third party could reconstruct prompts / outputs.
2) Please confirm Redwood's role: are you a processor for our request payloads and we (Subscribly) are the controller?
3) KMS: do you provide customer-managed keys (CMKs) with BYOK options, and are keys stored outside the customer region?
4) SCCs / DPA: please share your DPA draft and confirm whether you are willing to append SCCs for data transfers if needed.

We need short, precise answers we can include in our vendor risk doc. Thanks — if Marcus can chime in on key handling that would be great.

— Legal Ops
Subscribly
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Legal Ops <legal@subscribly.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-22T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question about where subscriber PII is processed

Hi — looping in Marcus (Security) and Priyom (SE) to provide concise answers and the DPA. Quick answers inline below — Marcus will provide the cryptographic/operational detail and a diagram.

1) Training / model weights: we do not share customer prompts or request payloads with external model training partners. Model development and weight updates occur on our internal infrastructure. No third-party training vendors have access to customer prompts.

2) Roles: Redwood acts as a processor for request payloads and any customer-specified data processed through our Hosted API. Customers are controllers. We document this in the DPA (attached).

3) KMS / CMK: we support customer-managed key (BYOK) options for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted API customers we offer envelope encryption with keys stored in our KMS; for enterprises we can arrange CMKs that are region-restricted and integrated with your KMS provider. Keys are not exported to subprocessors. Marcus will follow up with the key lifecycle diagram.

4) DPA / SCCs: attached is our standard DPA. We are willing to append SCCs where cross-border transfers occur; for Subscribly (US-based) most processing will remain in US regions unless you request EU residency.

Next steps: Marcus — can you attach a short KMS diagram and confirm backup deletion SLO? Priyom — can you book a 30-min call next week with the Subscribly legal / infra team if they want a live walkthrough?

Thanks,
Evelyn
